terms.grammar: pronoun: plural of is; genitive eōrum, eārum, dative and ablative eīs (iīs)
evidence: Liv. 5.41.9: ad eōs velut simulācra versī
Cic. Att. 6.1.12: Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur
terms.comment: Mostly left out as subject: amant inter sē, exercentur, they love each other, they play. For “them” as object, eōs, eās, ea (ad eōs … versī). In reported speech, “they” meaning the speakers is sē.

evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.61: ut illī efferuntur laetitiā, cum vīcērunt!
terms.comment: For a group set against another, or a new subject: nec ipse meōrum lūsibus nec illī studiīs meīs obstrepunt.
The people present or just named.

terms.grammar: interjection with the accusative: ecce with eōs, eās
terms.comment: Pointing them out; eccum, eccam for one.

phrases.latin: Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur, sed discunt, alter … frēnīs eget, alter calcāribus
phrases.english: The boys Cicero love each other, they play together, but they learn too; one … needs the reins, the other the spurs.

phrases.latin: ad eōs velut simulācra versī cum stārent
phrases.english: as they stood turned towards them as if towards statues

phrases.latin: nam nec ipse meōrum lūsibus nec illī studiīs meīs obstrepunt
phrases.english: for I don’t disturb my household’s games, nor they my work

phrases.latin: quanta studia dēcertantium sunt! quanta ipsa certāmina! ut illī efferuntur laetitiā, cum vīcērunt! ut pudet victōs! ut sē accūsārī nōlunt! quam cupiunt laudārī!
phrases.english: How keen the competitors are! How fierce the contests themselves! How carried away with joy they are when they have won! How ashamed the losers! How they hate to be blamed! How they long to be praised!

phrases.latin: Ostende hūc manūs. — Em tibi, ostendī, eccās.
phrases.english: Show me your hands. — There you are, I’ve shown them: here they are.

sources: Lewis & Short: is · Lewis & Short: ille · Lewis & Short: hic · Lewis & Short: ecce (eccum, eccōs)
